messages:
Lena Cho: Quick q for case study launch planning — can we put the partner logo alongside the customer logo on the customer story page? Partner is pushing for it as part of co-marketing. Want to make sure we’re not stepping on legal/brand landmines.

Camila Reyes: Do you mean like: Customer logo (Northwind) + Partner logo (e.g., “Acme Cloud Marketplace”) in the hero? Or partner logo somewhere lower as “integrates with”?

Lena Cho: Partner wants it in the hero area or at least above the fold. They’re saying “we’ll promote it if our logo is present.”

Soojin Lee: From messaging/PMM POV: hero with 2 logos reads like a joint case study / joint endorsement. We should be careful about implied partnership being the “reason” for outcomes (latency/cost/etc).

Rachel Kim: +1 from CS. Northwind is sensitive about vendor sprawl perception. If we add a 3rd party logo, we need explicit customer approval for that context.

Lena Cho: Totally. Partner argues it’s just brand credit since the deployment path is via their marketplace + their SI helped.

Michael Grant: Legal view: 3 separate permissions often get conflated here:
1) Customer permission for their own logo/quotes (we already handle)
2) Partner permission to use partner logo (separate brand permission)
3) Customer permission to associate *their* story with a third-party brand (often separate from #1)
If we do “partner logo next to customer logo” in a prominent way, we should treat it as #3 required.

Camila Reyes: Helpful. Our consent draft covers customer logo + quotes + attribution + optional metrics. It doesn’t explicitly say “we may display third-party partner logos alongside your story.”

Michael Grant: Right. Also: even if partner is asking for it, customer could later claim we implied they endorse partner (or that partner had access to their data). We need to be precise about what’s true.

Soojin Lee: Suggestion: keep hero as customer + Redwood only. Add a small “Deployed via: <Partner Marketplace>” line in the implementation section, with partner logo *there* (not equal weight with customer). More like an integration badge.

Markus Klein: Technically accurate version: “Purchased via <Partner Marketplace>” or “Deployed with <Partner> marketplace listing” is true for procurement, but doesn’t imply they operate the runtime. If the SI did architecture work, we can call them out as “Implementation partner” in a separate line.

Lena Cho: Partner wants something stronger than a text mention. They’ll probably be fine with logo in the “Implementation” block if it’s above the fold.

Camila Reyes: We can do a “Technology partners” / “Integrations” module on the page template (below summary, above deep dive). But we need consistent policy across stories.

Sofia Mendes: Contractually: do we have co-marketing terms/MOU with this partner already? If yes, check if it includes logo placement requirements + approval process. If not, we shouldn’t promise placement to close a one-off promo. Also, partner brand guidelines usually require specific clearspace/usage; they may require review/approval anyway.

Lena Cho: We have a marketplace partnership agreement, but I don’t think it says anything about being co-featured on customer stories.

Sofia Mendes: Then treat it as “optional, by mutual approval.” And we should require partner written approval of the exact usage (final page screenshot or PDF), plus customer approval of the association.

Michael Grant: +1. Separate approvals:
- Partner: logo usage approval (brand)
- Customer: association approval (context)
Also add guardrails: no language implying joint warranties, joint SLA, or partner endorsement of Redwood performance claims.

Soojin Lee: For copy: avoid “in partnership with <Partner>” on the case study page unless it’s truly a co-authored asset with signed terms.

Camila Reyes: Proposed path:
1) Hero: Customer + Redwood only
2) In “Solution” section: “Deployed via <Partner Marketplace>” with small partner logo (or “Available on <Partner Marketplace>”)
3) In footer: “Partner logo used with permission.” (If we need that line)
And we’ll add a one-line disclaimer that customer results are from Redwood deployment + config, not partner guarantee.

Rachel Kim: Works for CS as long as Northwind explicitly approves. We should put it in their review checklist so it’s not a surprise at the end.

Lena Cho: What does “explicitly approves” look like? Email ok?

Michael Grant: Email is acceptable if it’s clear + references the exact placement/context. Example: “You approve inclusion of <Partner> logo in the ‘Deployed via’ section of the Redwood customer story page describing your Redwood implementation.” Keep it attached to final proof.

Sofia Mendes: And partner should approve similarly. Also: if partner is getting a “promo commitment” (newsletter/social), make sure that’s in writing on our side with scope (1 post, 1 email mention, etc.)—otherwise it becomes open-ended.

Camila Reyes: Lena can you paste the partner ask verbatim? (so we don’t over-interpret)

Lena Cho: They said: “Happy to amplify the story through our marketplace newsletter + social, but we need our logo displayed alongside the customer on the story page and PDF.”

Soojin Lee: PDF is trickier. PDF often gets forwarded and could read like a joint collateral piece. I’d keep partner logo off the cover/first page. Put it on an inner page under “Deployment details” section.

Markus Klein: +1. We can include a small block: “Procurement channel: <Partner Marketplace>” with their logo. That’s factual.

Camila Reyes: Agree. If we put partner logo on PDF cover we’ll get into “co-branded asset” territory (and partner will want layout control).

Lena Cho: Ok, so:
- Web page: small partner logo in “Deployed via” module, not hero
- PDF: include in “Deployment details” section, not cover
And we’ll route for approvals.

Michael Grant: Yup. And if partner insists on cover/hero, we should treat it as a co-marketing deliverable with its own approval workflow + terms (and likely more time).

Camila Reyes: I’ll update our internal checklist for story approvals: add “3rd party logo present?” -> require customer + partner signoff. Tyler (ops) can add a field to intake later but for now we can track in the sheet.

Rachel Kim: Please also add a note on reference load / comms: partner should not directly contact the customer about the case study unless customer opts in. We’ve had that go sideways before.

Lena Cho: Good call. I’ll tell partner all comms go through Redwood unless customer explicitly agrees.

Soojin Lee: Also: keep claims clean. Don’t pair partner logo near performance metrics (“-37% $/1M tokens”) or it’ll look like partner is co-signing the numbers.

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup: I’ll loop in Ethan (writer) + Design ticket owner so we place the logo in a neutral spot.

Lena Cho: Thanks all. Next steps:
- I’ll ask partner for written approval for the exact usage (once we have proof)
- Camila/Rachel to confirm Northwind is ok w/ association
- Soojin to sanity check the copy line (“Deployed via…”)

Michael Grant: Add me when you have final proof; I’ll do a quick scan for implied endorsement language.

Camila Reyes: done. (also bookmarking this thread for the playbook)

Lena Cho: 🙏
